candidates.source_title: Improving Emergency Department Flow: Reducing Turnaround Time for Emergent CT Scans
candidates.locator: Abstract; Methods, intervention periods; Results; Discussion (schedule-ahead transport and order workflow)
candidates.source_setting: Large academic medical center adult emergency department, approximately 100,000 annual visits
candidates.source_period: Pre: July 1, 2015-March 1, 2016; post: July 1, 2017-March 1, 2018; intervention developed July 2016-July 2017
candidates.source_n: 10,063 CT orders in the eight-month pre-period; post-period order volume increased 13.8%; exact post count not stated in accessible text
candidates.source_evidence_basis: The observed baseline order-to-final-report TAT averaged 5.9 h (median 4.2 h) for 10,063 CT orders; an intervention bundle reduced TAT by 1.2 h in the corresponding post period despite 13.8% more orders (p<0.0001). The workflow crosses ED, transport, CT, and radiology handoffs; documented changes included communication, visual analytics, automation, education, and schedule-ahead transport to avoid batching transport requests.
candidates.limitations: Direct PubMed Central article access returned a verification wall, and the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returned HTTP 500 in this session. The values and workflow summary remain based on indexed article text pending direct primary-text inspection. Single-center bundled QI intervention; individual component effects cannot be isolated. The reported mean and median are not distributions.
candidates.inferred_scenario_use: Model imaging as order/protocoling, patient preparation, transport queue, scanner queue/acquisition, interpretation, preliminary/final report, with explicit handoffs and prioritization. Do not infer stage distributions from overall mean or median.
candidates.retrieval_timestamp_precision: day; time not logged during source inspection, midnight is a date placeholder
